q: 1. Hydrostatic pressure on a dam depends upon its ...............
explain: According to the hydrostatic law (P = ρgh), the pressure depends solely on the vertical depth below the free surface and the density of the liquid.

q: 2. Piezometers are used to measure ...............
options: pressure in water channels, pipes etc
difference in pressure at two points
explain: A piezometer is the simplest form of manometer used for measuring moderate pressures of liquids in pipes or containers.

q: 3. To measure very low pressure, we use ...............
explain: Piezometers are highly sensitive to small pressure changes because they use the height of the actual liquid column being measured.

q: 4. Gauge pressure is ...............
explain: Gauge pressure is measured relative to atmospheric pressure. Therefore, Absolute Pressure = Gauge Pressure + Atmospheric Pressure.

q: 5. Atmospheric pressure varies with ...............
explain: As altitude increases, the weight of the air above decreases, leading to a decrease in atmospheric pressure.

q: 6. Mercury is generally used in barometers because ...............
options: its vapour pressure is practically zero
the height of the barometer will be les
explain: Mercury's high density allows for a manageable column height (~760mm), and its low vapor pressure prevents error in the vacuum space.

q: 7. To avoid the force of surface tension in an inclined manometer, the minimum angle of inclination is ...............
explain: Standard practice in fluid mechanics suggests a minimum angle of 4 degrees to minimize the inaccuracies caused by surface tension/capillarity.

q: 8. The total pressure force on a plane area is equal to the area multiplied by the intensity of pressure at its centroid if ...............
explain: The total force F = P_avg × A. For any submerged plane, the average pressure occurs at the depth of the centroid (h_bar), regardless of orientation.

q: 9. The centre of pressure of a vertical plane immersed in a liquid is at ...............
explain: The center of pressure (h_p) is always located below the centroid of the area because pressure increases with depth.

q: 10. The depth of the centre of pressure on a vertical rectangular gate (4 m wide, 3 m high) with water upto top surface is ...............
explain: For a rectangle of height 'h' with the top at the surface, the center of pressure is at (2/3)h. (2/3) * 3m = 2.0m.

q: 11. On an inclined plane, centre of pressure is located ...............
explain: Similar to a vertical plane, the pressure distribution is deeper at the bottom, shifting the resultant force (center of pressure) below the centroid.

q: 12. When a body is totally or partially immersed in a fluid it is buoyed up by a force equal to ...............
options: weight of the fluid displaced by the body
weight of the body and fluid displaced by the body
difference of weights of the fluid displaced and that on the body
explain: This is Archimedes' Principle, which defines the buoyant force as the weight of the volume of fluid that the body displaces.

q: 13. A floating body attains stable equilibrium if its metacentre is ...............
explain: Stability is achieved when the Metacentre (M) is above the Centre of Gravity (G). If M is above G, a restoring couple is formed.

q: 14. Centre of buoyancy is ...............
options: centroid of pressure of the displaced liquid
explain: The center of buoyancy is the point through which the upward buoyant force acts, coinciding with the geometric center (centroid) of the displaced liquid volume.

q: 15. A water tank partially filled with water is being carried on a truck moving with a constant horizontal acceleration. The level of the water ...............
options: rises on the front side of the tank
falls on the back side of the tank
remains the same at both sides of the tank
rises on the back side and falls on the front side
explain: The inertia of the water causes it to move toward the rear of the tank, resulting in a higher water level at the back and a lower level at the front.

q: 16. For mountaneous regions having steep slope, wagons for carrying liquid are made with bottom ...............
explain: Keeping the bottom horizontal ensures that the liquid remains stable relative to gravity and reduces the risk of spills or excessive pressure on the tank ends.

q: 17. A cylindrical vessel 40 cm high is revolved about its vertical axis so that the water touches the bottom when it just spills out. If the radius of the cylinder if √5 cm, the angular velocity of rotation is ...............
explain: Using the vortex formula h = (ω²r²)/(2g). Given h = 0.4m, r = √0.05m. Solving for ω gives approximately 2 rad/sec (assuming g is 10).

q: 18. The rise of the liquid along the walls of a revolving cylinder above the initial level, is ...............
options: greater than the depression of the liquid at the axis of rotation
lesser than the depression of the liquid at the axis of rotation
the same as the depression of the liquid at the axis of rotation
explain: In a forced vortex (solid body rotation), the volume of the paraboloid of revolution is half the volume of the circumscribing cylinder, meaning rise = fall.

q: 19. When a liquid rotates at constant angular velocity about a vertical axis of a rigid body, the pressure ...............
options: increases linearly to its radial distance
varies inversely as the altitude along any vertical line
varies as the square of the radial distance
decreases as the square of the radial distance
explain: The pressure head in a forced vortex increases with the square of the radius (v²/2g = ω²r²/2g).

q: 20. The imaginary line drawn such that the tangents at its all points indicate the direction of the velocity of the fluid particles at each point, is called ...............
explain: A streamline is a curve that is everywhere tangent to the instantaneous local velocity vector.

q: 21. If velocities of fluid particles vary from point to point in magnitude and direction, as well as form instant to instant, the flow is said to be ...............
explain: Turbulent flow is characterized by chaotic changes in pressure and flow velocity, varying both in space and time.

q: 22. An ideal flow of a liquid obeys ...............
explain: All fluid flows, including ideal (non-viscous, incompressible) flows, must satisfy the principle of conservation of mass, represented by the continuity equation.

q: 23. The acceleration f required to accelerate a rectangular tank containing water horizontally so that the slope of its free surface is 45°, is ...............
explain: Since tan θ = a/g, and tan 45° = 1, then a/g = 1, which means the acceleration (f) must equal g.

q: 24. The flow in which each liquid particle has a definite path and the paths of adjacent particles do not cross each other, is called ...............
explain: In streamline (or laminar) flow, fluid particles move in smooth layers or paths without macroscopic mixing.

q: 25. To avoid the tendency of separation of liquid flow, the most suitable ratio of the diameters of the throat and the pipe, is ...............
explain: A throat diameter ratio between 1/3 and 1/2 is standard to balance sensitivity of pressure measurement with the prevention of cavitation/separation.

q: 26. The velocity of the fluid particle at the centre of the paper section, is ...............
explain: In pipe flow, especially laminar, the velocity profile is parabolic with the maximum velocity occurring at the centerline.

q: 27. A fluid particle may possess the displacement or ...............
explain: Fluid motion can involve translation (moving), rotation (spinning), and deformation/distortion (changing shape).

q: 28. An independent mass of a fluid does not posses ...............
explain: A fluid in motion potentially possesses all three forms of energy: potential (elevation), kinetic (velocity), and pressure energy.

q: 29. The differential equation dp/ρ + gdz + vdv = 0 for a fluid motion is suggested by ...............
explain: This is Euler's equation of motion. When integrated along a streamline, it yields the Bernoulli equation.

q: 30. The line joining the points to which the liquid rises in vertical piezometer tubes fitted at different cross-section of a conduit, is known as ...............
options: pressure grade line or hydraulic grade line
explain: The Hydraulic Grade Line (HGL) represents the sum of the pressure head and datum head (P/w + z) along the pipeline.

q: 31. From a nozzle exposed to atmosphere, the liquid jet traverses ...............
explain: A free jet acts as a projectile; under the influence of gravity, its trajectory follows a parabolic path.

q: 32. The ratio of the maximum height to which a jet inclined through θ rises to its total horizontal span is ...............
explain: Maximum height H = (u² sin²θ)/2g and Range R = (u² sin2θ)/g. The ratio H/R simplifies to 1/4 tan θ.

q: 33. A jet projected at an angle of 45°, 40 m from the foot of a vertical column, just reaches the top of the column. The height of the column is ...............
explain: Using the trajectory equation y = x tanθ - [gx² / (2u² cos²θ)]. For a project reaching its max height at 40m distance at 45°, the height is 20m.

q: 34. When the whole fluid mass rotates either due to fluid pressure or gravity or rotation previously imparted, the motion is known as ...............
explain: In a free vortex, fluid rotates without external torque (like water draining from a bathtub). External energy is not continuously applied.

q: 35. The dimensionless parameter not applicable to flowing liquids, is ...............
explain: Kinematic viscosity (ν) has units of m²/s; it is a physical property, not a dimensionless parameter.

q: 36. For the flow of liquid from an open ended tube (or nozzle) leading to the formation of spray of liquid drops, the number generally applied, is ...............
explain: Weber number (We) relates inertial force to surface tension, which is the dominant force in drop formation and atomization.

q: 37. A piezometer opening in pipes measures ...............
explain: A piezometer tube measures the static pressure (P/w) at the point of connection.

q: 38. Hydraulic ram is a device ...............
options: for lifting water without an electric motor
explain: A hydraulic ram uses the energy of a large quantity of water falling through a small height to lift a small quantity of water to a much greater height without external power.

q: 39. An ideal fluid ...............
explain: An ideal fluid is a theoretical concept where the fluid has no viscosity (frictionless) and is perfectly incompressible.

q: 40. Though angle of deviation of liquid is more in internal mouth piece, the contraction of the jet, is
options: more in the internal mouth piece
less in the internal mouth piece
explain: In a Borda’s (internal) mouthpiece running full, the coefficient of contraction is actually higher (less contraction of the final jet) compared to when it's running free.

q: 41. The intensity of pressure due to sudden closure of a valve... is directly proportional to ...............
options: square root of the bulk modulus
explain: The pressure rise ($p$) due to water hammer is given by $p = ho v C$, where the wave velocity $C$ is $\sqrt{K/ho}$. Thus, pressure is proportional to $\sqrt{K}$ (square root of bulk modulus).

q: 42. The horizontal component of the force on a curved surface is equal to ...............
options: weight of liquid vertically below the surface
force on a vertical projection of the curved surface
product of pressure at its centroid and the area
weight of liquid retained by the curved area
explain: The horizontal component of hydrostatic force on any curved surface is the same as the force exerted on a vertical plane surface formed by the projection of the curved surface.

q: 43. In order to avoid capillary correction, the minimum diameter of a manometer for measuring pressure should be....
explain: To minimize the effect of surface tension (capillary rise or depression), the glass tube of a manometer should have an internal diameter of at least 6 mm.

q: 44. If H is the depth of water retained by a vertical wall, the height of centre of pressure above the bottom is ...............
explain: The centre of pressure for a rectangular surface (vertical wall) is at $2/3 H$ from the top, which is $1/3 H$ (H/3) from the bottom.

q: 45. The moment of inertia of a floating body... are I and V respectively. The height of the metacentre above centre of buoyancy of the body, is ...............
explain: The distance between the centre of buoyancy (B) and the metacentre (M) is known as the BM distance, calculated as $BM = I/V$.

q: 46. The radius of gyration of the water line... is 4 m and its metacentric height is 72.5 cm. The period of oscillation of the ship, is ...............
explain: The time period of oscillation is $T = 2\pi \sqrt{k^2 / (g \cdot GM)}$. Using $k=4$, $GM=0.725$, and $g=9.81$, $T$ calculates roughly to $3\pi$.

q: 47. The equation τ = μ (dv/dy) for the viscosity, is suggested ...............
explain: This is Newton's Law of Viscosity, where shear stress is proportional to the rate of shear strain (velocity gradient).

q: 48. An open container filled with water is moved vertically upward with a uniform linear acceleration. The pressure at its bottom will be ...............
explain: The effective acceleration becomes $(g + a)$. Therefore, the pressure $P = ho(g+a)h$, which is greater than the static pressure $ho gh$.

q: 49. An open container filled with water is moved vertically downward with a uniform linear acceleration. The pressure at its bottom will be ...............
explain: The effective acceleration becomes $(g - a)$. Therefore, the pressure $P = ho(g-a)h$, which is less than the static pressure.

q: 50. Cavitation is caused by ...............
explain: Cavitation occurs when the local pressure in a liquid drops below its vapor pressure, causing vapor bubbles to form and then collapse violently.
